title: Karma Squirrel
text: It was one day amid torture that gradually escalated, I say.
“Guuuuuuh……”
“P-please stop! If you do any more than that, she’ll die!”
The torture inflicted upon Mole, who had nursed him, grew savage indeed, and the noble finally drew out a blade, stabbing her in places that avoided vital points on purpose.
“Fuhahaha… scream more! It seems you trust this slave of yours a great deal, don’t you? How about this—if you kill her yourself, I’ll set you free?”

Faced with such a devilish proposal, Itsuki stared at Mole, trembling. Itsuki said that somewhere in his heart, something whispered to him. One voice told him to lay hands on Mole for the sake of ease, for the sake of freedom. But he immediately shook off that thought, deciding that no matter what, such words could never be accepted. He was, after all, someone chosen to be a Hero. There was no way he’d ever make such a choice. And yet, at the same time, an endless fury was steadily seizing control of his heart. Mole, still hanging bound with her arms behind her back, smiled at Itsuki.
“Itsuki-san… please… set me… free…”

Kill me. If you do that, then… Itsuki heard that plea escape her lips. No matter how you looked at it, there was no way this noble would ever actually free her. Even though she surely knew that perfectly well, Mole still offered Itsuki that cruel proposal, clinging to some faint sliver of hope.
“I won’t do that!”
Itsuki declared that he still wouldn’t take that step, glaring at the noble with hatred welling up from the depths of his heart.
“Tch! How boring! Then I’ll kill her myself! Despair to your heart’s content! Hahahahaha!”

And so the noble gripped his sword, drawing back his arm to plunge it into Mole’s heart. Thu-dump! Itsuki’s heart pounded with sudden, overwhelming force, and time itself seemed to slow to a crawl, or so he said.
——Do you want power?

Ah… such vile, endlessly cruel, unforgivable evil existed right before him, and even in such a dire crisis, no one was coming to help. What was justice, really? Wasn’t this exactly the kind of situation where an ally of justice should come to the rescue? Not even back in Japan, when he’d suffered such vicious discrimination for having low stats, had he ever felt like this.
——Do you hate everything?
That’s right… if an ally of justice wasn’t going to appear at this very moment, then “justice” must be nothing more than a figment of the imagination.

『I believed in something so utterly worthless—a justice that couldn’t even save the one irreplaceable person standing right in front of me… Yes, then I’ll cast aside such justice. From here on, I’ll act on my own ego, doing only what I want to do. For that purpose… no matter what sins I must commit, even if I’m called not a Hero but a Demon Lord—there is someone I want to save!』

Thus Itsuki resolved to leap over the line he’d sworn never to cross within his heart, cast aside the notion of justice he’d once held, and surrender himself to his rage. All of it, he said, was born of fury at a world that allowed such things to happen.

Well… it’s an understandable reason, I say. Yes indeed—since Father is normally such a gentle soul, I imagine drawing out that kind of wrath from him must be terribly difficult. I suppose Itsuki, too, had come to realize the truth of this kingdom. Even I hadn’t expected the Armor lot to sell Itsuki out in such a short span of time. I’d figured, at most, they’d start passing blame around amongst themselves and fall apart, and Itsuki would merely come to realize how ugly they truly were.

However, thinking back on my meeting with Ark, I get the sense—vaguely—that recklessly drawing out something called Wrath probably isn’t a good thing. In the original world, Father eventually stopped relying on the power of Wrath before he finally defeated the Crimson Swine’s true form, but if he’d kept drawing on it the whole way through… who knows what might have happened. Incidentally, according to Rival, Father—having been unable to save people from false accusations, starting with that first world—apparently carries about him something dragons find exceedingly pleasant. Infuriating as it is, that’s all the more reason Father must never be allowed to bear the Curse of Wrath, I say.
With a whoosh, black flames erupted around Itsuki, who’d been bound hand and foot and unable to move, and the shackles melted away.
“Iron Maiden.”
He’d thought this newly acquired skill might come in handy here, but since its activation conditions displayed themselves, he used it right away.
“Bind Arrow!”
Thud! An arrow suddenly shot out from the noble’s shadow just as he moved to finish off Mole, binding him in place. It was a skill that could be fired without even drawing a bow.
“Ugh!? Wh-what—!?”

Struck by the sudden binding arrow, the noble’s eyes went wide as he turned to face Itsuki. Swaying, Itsuki rose to his feet, murderous intent flooding him unchecked. And in his hands he gripped the Bow of Wrath—a member of the Curse series. I myself am capable of triggering a similar transformation. It manifested when Filolial-sama was killed by Phoenix, but thanks to Filo-tan and Father, I’ve managed to keep from ever using it, I say. Naturally, it did grow stronger after what Takt did to me. The moment the bow transformed, changes began appearing across Itsuki’s body as well—his body hair turning black, apparently. Incidentally, from what I understand, using a Curse series weapon while in fairy form temporarily makes the hat disappear, turns everything black, and alters one’s physique. It seems to result in a transformation resembling one of those Karma-type bosses that appear in activation zones.
“Wh-what are you doing! How dare you pull something like this! That collar will slice your head clean off!”
Grrrr! The collar around Itsuki’s neck began rapidly tightening in response to his harming the noble, but Itsuki, having activated his Curse, simply gripped the collar—and it shattered to pieces.
“What a pathetically weak collar. To think… I was ever tormented by something like this.”
He looked down upon the thing that had once bound his weaker self, with utter contempt, or so it’s said.
There was no ally of justice. And yet, he wanted to save this person.

Not two people tomorrow, not three people in the future, not countless people in some far-off future. Right now, he would destroy the evil standing before him and save this one person, who even now seemed on the verge of fading away into nothing.

Not righteousness, not righteous fury. Not some fate handed down by others, not being the Hero who saves the world from waves of catastrophe. Even if his own head were to fly off and he breathed his last in the very next moment, that would be fine. If he could save this person right now, then tomorrow, the future, a happy ending… he wanted none of it. If only he could become the kind of person capable of that—so Itsuki said.
“Wha…”

Faced with how effortlessly the collar had shattered and with his own predicament, the noble finally, at last, understood his situation. His face paled, twisting with terror at the sight of Itsuki, hatred billowing up from within him.
“Terror Flame, Agony Shock!”
“Gh, aaaaah……! Gyaaaaah!? Aaaaaaaah!?”
Itsuki unleashed a fear-amplifying skill upon the noble, setting him ablaze and then, with a pain-enhancing debuff, sent him writhing in agony.
“I-I’m going to die!? S-somebody! Somebody help me! Aaaah, this slave—! Do you think you’ll get away with a slave doing something like this!? Aaaaaaah! J-just spare my life—”
“Hahahahaha! How pathetic. After torturing us that much, you can’t even endure this much pain? What you did was far worse than this, you know?”

Even as he felt himself nearly swallowed whole by the hatred and rage bubbling up from the depths of his heart, Itsuki approached the weakened, barely-conscious Mole—her trembling mouth still urging him with her eyes to stop—and checked on her condition. In that instant, his reason recalled the gentle expression she’d worn while nursing him, and it reined in the fury stirred by the Bow of Wrath, pulling it back to a controllable level.
“Guooooh, how dare you do such a thing… that woman—”
Thock! Itsuki drew his bow and, just as the noble tried to threaten him by activating Mole’s slave brand, sent an arrow straight through the noble’s cheek, pinning it shut.
“Shut up. Stop making that rotten noise. It’s disgusting.”
“Aga—!? Guh!?”
With his mouth pinned shut, the noble’s eyes rolled wildly, or so it’s said.

“Now then, it’s time for you to end. Every second you remain alive is disgusting to me. I’d love to torment you further and watch you suffer, but I’ll settle my grudge by killing as many scum like you as I possibly can instead. So then… drop dead.”

From now on, he would do as he pleased—living such a selfish life meant he couldn’t hope for a proper death himself, Itsuki supposedly thought. So he decided that until the day he himself perished, he would drag as many scum like this noble down with him as he could. And so, though Itsuki had never killed a human being until now, he unleashed his skill, driven by murderous intent welling up from the very depths of his soul.

『The name of the punishment I have decreed for this foolish sinner is a single strike that pierces the whole body in the embrace of an iron maiden. Even your screams shall be embraced—writhe in agony!』
“Iron Maiden!”

The moment he finished the incantation, the same torture device that Father himself had once used was summoned, opening to envelop the noble before closing shut again. Itsuki apparently heard the sound of the binding arrow shattering.
“Rot in hell!”
Flaring up in response to Itsuki’s wrath, the Iron Maiden blazed and burst apart, and the noble, pierced through by countless spikes, breathed his last.
